newsitem.title: USA: Xerox files patent infringement suit.
newsitem.headline: Xerox files patent infringement suit.

text.p: Xerox Corp. said Wednesday it sued U.S. Robotics Corp. over the modem maker's popular Pilot hand-held computer and its Graffiti handwriting recognition software, accusing the company of patent infringement.
The lawsuit was filed Monday in U.S. District Court in Rochester, N.Y., Xerox said.
Xerox is seeking an injunction to halt sales of the Pilot without a license for the disputed technology, plus unspecified damages.
"Until we're served with the suit, we'll have no comment," said Sara Powers, a spokeswoman for Skokie, Ill.-based U.S. Robotics.
The Pilot, a simple computer that holds information like schedules and contacts, is the most popular of a class of devices known as personal digital assistants, or PDAs.
At issue is a Xerox patent for handwriting recognition technology known as Unistrokes, which was invented at the Xerox Palo Alto (Calif.) Research Centre in 1993, Stamford, Conn.-based Xerox said.

The patent, issued last January, covers the use and recognition of handwritten text using an alphabet system designed especially for reliable recognition in pen computers, thus eliminating much of the ambiguity of prior computerized handwriting recognition systems, Xerox said.

Xerox alleged in its lawsuit that a vice president at Palm Computing, now a subsidiary of U.S. Robotics, had approached Xerox for information about licensing the Unistrokes technology after reading an article about it.
Although he was told Xerox had a patent pending on Unistrokes, Xerox alleged U.S. Robotics adopted it without obtaining a license.
When the patent was issued, it was immediately brought to U.S. Robotics' attention and, although the company talked with Xerox, it failed to obtain a license, Xerox said.
In addition to being a major power in the photocopier business, Xerox has pioneered a number of information technologies.
U.S. Robotics, the biggest maker of consumer computer modems, is being acquired by computer network company 3Com Corp.
Xerox stock rose $1.50 to $61.625 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. U.S. Robotics rose $1.25 to $51 on the Nasdaq.
